## Objective

This section illustrates how the model can be used to compare six application strategies across a common set of fertiliser scenarios. The strategies are broadcast application (`bc`), broadcast application followed by immediate deep incorporation, band spreading with trailing hoses (`bsth`), trailing shoe (`ts`), open-slot injection (`os`), and closed-slot injection (`cs`).

## Setup

```{python}
from itertools import product
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter
import pandas as pd

from nh3pred import predict
```

## Define the scenarios

The scenarios are defined by combining different values of fertiliser origin, application rate and applied TAN, dry matter, and fertiliser pH. For the numerical variables, the values below are the quantiles calculated from the training data used to fit the model. For `tan_app` and `app_rate`, values at the same quantile level are paired. The full factorial design combines:

- cattle and pig fertiliser origins;
- paired 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of applied TAN and application rate;
- the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of dry matter and fertiliser pH;
- the six application strategies.

This gives 324 predictions: 54 fertiliser scenarios for each strategy.

All other inputs, including crop, tillage, and soil type, are omitted and completed with the package defaults.

```{python}
quantile_levels = [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]
quantiles = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "tan_app": [43.68, 68.59, 106.20],
        "app_rate": [26.67, 35.00, 45.74],
        "fer_dm": [3.4, 5.5, 7.4],
        "fer_ph": [7.10, 7.35, 7.70],
    },
    index=quantile_levels,
)

method_settings = [
    ("bc", "bc", "none", None),
    ("bc + deep\nincorp.", "bc", "deep", 0.05),
    ("bsth", "bsth", "none", None),
    ("ts", "ts", "none", None),
    ("os", "os", "none", None),
    ("cs", "cs", "none", None),
]

rows = []
for fer_origin, pair_q, dm_q, ph_q, method in product(
    ["cat", "pig"],
    quantile_levels,
    quantile_levels,
    quantile_levels,
    method_settings,
):
    method_label, app_method, incorp, time_incorp = method
    rows.append(
        {
            "fer_origin": fer_origin,
            "tan_app": quantiles.loc[pair_q, "tan_app"],
            "app_rate": quantiles.loc[pair_q, "app_rate"],
            "fer_dm": quantiles.loc[dm_q, "fer_dm"],
            "fer_ph": quantiles.loc[ph_q, "fer_ph"],
            "app_method": app_method,
            "incorp": incorp,
            "time_incorp": time_incorp,
            "method": method_label,
            "tan_app_rate_quantile": pair_q,
            "fer_dm_quantile": dm_q,
            "fer_ph_quantile": ph_q,
        }
    )

pdat = pd.DataFrame(rows)
pdat.insert(0, "id", range(1, len(pdat) + 1))
pdat.iloc[:,:8].head()
```

## Generate predictions

No time-dependent data are supplied, predictions are made using the default time sequence and weather profiles. The output column `prediction_erel` is the predicted cumulative emission divided by the applied TAN.

```{python}
predictions = predict(pdat)

predictions[
    [
        "id",
        "ct",
        "app_method",
        "incorp",
        "prediction_ecum",
        "prediction_erel",
    ]
].head()
```

## Compare relative emissions at 240h

For each scenario, only the prediction at 240 hours is retained. Each box therefore summarises the same 54 combinations of fertiliser origin and numerical predictor values used to define the scenarios.

```{python}
cumulative_predictions = (
    predictions.sort_values("ct")
    .groupby("id", as_index=False)
    .tail(1)
)

method_order = [setting[0] for setting in method_settings]
colors = ["#0072B2", "#56B4E9", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7"]


def plot_cumulative_emissions(cumulative_predictions, title):
    boxplot_data = [
        cumulative_predictions.loc[
            cumulative_predictions["method"].eq(method), "prediction_erel"
        ]
        for method in method_order
    ]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.5))
    boxes = ax.boxplot(
        boxplot_data,
        tick_labels=method_order,
        patch_artist=True,
        showfliers=True,
    )
    for box, color in zip(boxes["boxes"], colors):
        box.set_facecolor(color)
        box.set_alpha(0.75)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
    ax.set(
        xlabel="Application strategy",
        ylabel="Relative emission at 240h (% of applied TAN)",
        title=title,
    )
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=20)
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


plot_cumulative_emissions(
    cumulative_predictions,
    "Relative emissions at 240 h across application strategies",
)
```

## Compare emission dynamics

The panels below show all scenario trajectories for each application strategy. Thin lines represent individual combinations of fertiliser origin and numerical predictor values, while thick lines show the median trajectory for cattle and pig fertilisers.

```{python}
def plot_emission_dynamics(predictions):
    origins = {
        "cat": ("Cattle", "#0072B2"),
        "pig": ("Pig", "#D55E00"),
    }
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        2,
        3,
        figsize=(13, 8),
        sharex=True,
        sharey=True,
    )

    for ax, method in zip(axes.flat, method_order):
        method_data = predictions.loc[predictions["method"].eq(method)]
        for origin, (label, color) in origins.items():
            origin_data = method_data.loc[
                method_data["fer_origin"].eq(origin)
            ]
            for _, trajectory in origin_data.groupby("id", sort=False):
                trajectory = trajectory.sort_values("ct")
                ax.plot(
                    trajectory["ct"],
                    trajectory["prediction_erel"],
                    color=color,
                    alpha=0.12,
                    linewidth=0.8,
                )

            median = origin_data.groupby("ct", as_index=False)[
                "prediction_erel"
            ].median()
            ax.plot(
                median["ct"],
                median["prediction_erel"],
                color=color,
                linewidth=2.5,
                label=label,
            )

        ax.set_title(method.replace("\n", " "))
        ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.5)
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
        ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    for ax in axes[-1, :]:
        ax.set_xlabel("Time since application (h)")
    fig.supylabel(
        "Relative emissions (% of applied TAN)",
        x=0.01,
    )
    handles, labels = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        labels,
        loc="lower center",
        ncols=2,
        frameon=False,
        bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.01),
    )
    fig.suptitle(
        "Predicted ammonia-emission dynamics by application strategy",
        fontsize=16,
        y=0.98,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.07, 1, 0.95])
    plt.show()


plot_emission_dynamics(predictions)
```
